question.prompt: Suppose \(z\) is a complex number with positive imaginary part, with real part greater than \(1,\) and with \(|z| = 2.\) In the complex plane, the four points \(0,\) \(z,\) \(z^2,\) and \(z^3\) are the vertices of a quadrilateral with area \(15.\) What is the imaginary part of \(z?\)

solutions.title: Compare similar triangles
solutions.explanation:
Multiplication by \(z\) doubles lengths and rotates through a fixed angle, so it multiplies triangle areas by \(4\).

Let \(O,U,A,B,C\) represent the complex numbers \(0,1,z,z^2,z^3\), respectively, and write \(b=\operatorname{Im}(z)>0\). If \(\theta\) is the angle from the positive real axis to \(OA\), then
\[
z=2(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta).
\]
The conditions on the real and imaginary parts give \(0<\theta<60^\circ\). Consequently, the rays \(OA,OB,OC\) have angles \(\theta,2\theta,3\theta\), in that order within the upper half-plane. The diagonal \(OB\) splits the quadrilateral into the nonoverlapping triangles \(OAB\) and \(OBC\).

Triangle \(OUA\) has base \(OU=1\) and height \(b\), so its area is \(b/2\). Multiplication by \(z\) sends \(OUA\) to \(OAB\), and then sends \(OAB\) to \(OBC\). Since the length scale factor is \(2\), the area scale factor is \(2^2=4\). Thus
\[
[OAB]=4\cdot\frac b2=2b,
\qquad
[OBC]=4\cdot2b=8b.
\]
The given area therefore yields
\[
15=2b+8b=10b,
\qquad b=\frac32.
\]
This is feasible: the positive real part is \(\sqrt{4-9/4}=\sqrt7/2>1\). The imaginary part is \(\boxed{\frac32}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

solutions.title: Coordinate area products
solutions.explanation:
The coordinate products used in the area formula simplify nicely for consecutive powers of \(z\).

Write \(z=a+bi\), where \(a>1\), \(b>0\), and \(a^2+b^2=4\). Set
\[
u=a^2-b^2,\qquad v=2ab.
\]
Then the points corresponding to \(z,z^2,z^3\) are
\[
A=(a,b),\qquad B=(u,v),\qquad
C=(au-bv,av+bu).
\]
Also,
\[
u^2+v^2=(a^2+b^2)^2=16.
\]
For points \(P=(p_x,p_y)\) and \(Q=(q_x,q_y)\), define
\[
D(P,Q)=p_xq_y-p_yq_x.
\]
The triangle case of the shoelace formula says that \([OPQ]=\frac12|D(P,Q)|\). The sign of \(D(P,Q)\) also indicates which side of the directed line \(OP\) contains \(Q\).

Here,
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(A,B)&=av-bu\\
&=2a^2b-b(a^2-b^2)\\
&=b(a^2+b^2)=4b,
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
D(B,C)&=u(av+bu)-v(au-bv)\\
&=b(u^2+v^2)=16b.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(D(B,A)=-4b<0\) and \(D(B,C)=16b>0\), points \(A\) and \(C\) lie on opposite sides of \(OB\). The two triangles along this diagonal therefore have disjoint interiors and together form the quadrilateral. Its area is
\[
15=\frac12(4b+16b)=10b.
\]
Thus \(b=3/2\), with the required real part \(a=\sqrt7/2>1\). The answer is \(\boxed{\frac32}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
